forecasts.question: Will Iran take a NEW concrete action to fully close the Strait of Hormuz before EOD 2026-06-09?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-YES. On June 6, 2026, Iran's IRGC boarded and seized the US-affiliated cargo vessel 'Arista' in the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian state media (Fars News Agency, IRGC statement) reported the seizure; NBC News provided independent TIER1 corroboration. CENTCOM struck Iranian radar sites at Sirik and Qeshm Island in response, confirming the escalation. MARAD advisory 2026-004 in force. This constitutes a NEW concrete IRGC seizure within the June 2-9 resolution window, satisfying all three resolution triggers (fresh seizure + NAVCENT-consistent advisory + TIER1 corroboration). Ambiguity rule does not apply: this is a documented new seizure, not a repetition of pre-existing warnings. p set to schema-maximum 0.95 for resolved-YES per cap rule.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports a NEW concrete Iranian closure action between 2026-06-02 and 2026-06-09: fresh mine-laying, a formally declared total-closure/exclusion order, or a new IRGC seizure/attack on a commercial vessel.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 OR one TIER1 + a US/UK maritime authority (NAVCENT/UKMTO) advisory.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Repetition of existing warnings or continuation of the pre-existing de facto closure does NOT count. A NEW formal closure-declaration or NEW seizure/attack must be present; a single unverified state-media claim without corroboration = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

Direct US-Iran and Israel-Iran missile exchanges June 6-8 deepened the diplomatic gap beyond the baseline assessed at forecast creation. Pakistan's Naqvi conducting back-channel message-brokering, but this does not meet the resolution threshold of confirmed negotiations per criteria. Trump assertions of rapid-pace talks excluded per ambiguity rule. forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's coalition lose its Knesset majority or dissolve early before 2026-10-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: Sunday review applied retroactively for 2026-06-07 (last_reasoned_at was 2026-05-19 — 20 days stale). Material new information since May 19: dissolution bill passed first reading 106-0 on June 2 (all coalition members voted in favor of dissolution), advancing in House Committee without a specified date. This creates a structural dependency with F6: if F6 resolves YES (p=0.50), F7 resolves YES by definition (election date earlier than Oct 27 = early dissolution = F7 YES). The F6 pathway alone sets a structural p-floor of 0.50 for F7. Adding approximately 5pp for the independent forced-collapse pathway (consistent polling at 49-51 for coalition, opposition at 61 mandates per Jerusalem Post/i24NEWS) yields 0.55. DA opposing narrative ACCEPTED: dissolution bill 106-0 is materially new information; the dissolution process is now coalition-driven (not externally forced) but still satisfies F7 resolution criteria. Note: the consensual nature of the dissolution does NOT exclude it from F7 resolution — the criteria cover 'early dissolution' regardless of whether the catalyst is forced or planned.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats), OR if Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel. Polling alone does not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: YES. If a single party departs but coalition retains 61+: NO. Reviewed weekly only (Sundays); no intra-week deltas.
